threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'shopping trolley' instead of a 'bag for life' like everyone else. The locals can spot that a mile away.
Last night, a guy on the 333 claimed the bus was his own personal Uber and refused to get off at the terminus. Classic Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a stray cat casually lounging on a graffiti-covered bench, a hipster sipping coffee beside it, and a kid practicing skate tricks nearby. Perfectly Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Döner shop that also sells homemade Turkish desserts. Late night snack and sweet cravings solved in one stop.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how we speed past that BART Civic Center station mess without a second glance, while the newbies are still looking for maps.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading commuters with a ukulele at Civic Center this morning. Muni delays couldn't overshadow his sunny vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll down Carrer Gran de Gràcia and find a table without a booking. Wrong! Those hidden gems fill up fast with locals.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newbie by their awkward attempts at navigating the Mercat de la Llibertat—they're the ones overly enthusiastic about the anchovies.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of just 'the overground' when you're on the local trains. Everyone else just rolls their eyes.
Caught the 196 last night, and two guys were debating whether the dodgy kebab shop was worth the risk. Classic Brixton buzz at 2 AM.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I heard the sound of a street musician playing accordion while a couple argued over a döner. Pure Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how every summer, random folks set up disco parties in the parks after dusk? Just bring a speaker and dance under the stars—totally Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they have a favorite street vendor for tacos but still roll their eyes at the line for taquerias on weekends.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Witnessed a guy juggling on the bus to the sound of a saxophonist outside. Only in the Tenderloin does chaos feel like a warm embrace.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just for trendy bars, but locals know the real charm is in the quiet side streets where old men play dominoes.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their excitement over the first patatas bravas at a tourist trap, still untouched by the dive bar scene down the street.
